full_judgment: 4. The provisions of section 367 Crl.P.C. were not strictly followed by the learned Magistrate, but the main points in this case under sections 379 and 147 of the Penal Code are found to have been duly considered by the learned Magistrate. His order shows that the disputed land was a khas land of the Government but both the parties claimed right, title and possession thereof. The learned Magistrate also considered the R.S. Khatian which shows that the disputed land was a homestead land. The evidence of D.W. 1 shows that the accused persons were living in their houses on the disputed land. P.W. 1 the complainant claimed to have taken settlement of the land from the Sub-Divisional Officer by paying necessary dues and he has been corroborated on this claim by the Tahshilder, P.W.6. But the Tahshilder did not say anything about possession, that is, he did not say that after the settlement possession was delivered to the com peasant. Moreover, evidence of P.W. 1, the complainant, as reproduced in the Paper-book, does not show that any paddy was removed from the land by the accused. P.W. 1 simply stated that the accused persons damaged the Aush paddy. As such the charge of theft necessarily falls through. The only charge then remains is that of rioting. The learned Magistrate observed that on consideration of the evidence he found that the prosecution failed to prove the case. The High Court Division, in the circumstances, rightly observed that though judgment of the Magistrate was not in proper form some reasons have been given for acquitting the accused persons. We do not think that any miscarriage of justice has been caused by non-compliance with the provisions of S. 367 Cr. P.C.
